subject: Optumia - invoice itemization + proposed commit structure
messages:
From: Elena Silva <elena.silva@optumia.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@optumia.com, David Porter <david.porter@optumia.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Billing export and committed tiers — next steps

Hi Logan,

Thanks for yesterday's demo. Procurement needs two items to move this forward: a) a sample export from Redwood that shows per-token line items (timestamp, user_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, cost) and b) a simple committed-tier pricing table we can circulate internally that shows effective per-token rates at 3 commit levels (100M, 500M, 2B tokens).

We have a finance review on Friday. Can you provide the sample export (anonymized is fine) and the proposed commit tiers + any caveats about burst usage or overage handling? Also let us know how invoice line items would appear if we requested token-level visibility vs. summarized daily totals.

Elena
Procurement — Optumia Health

[Attachment: optumia_usage_sample.csv (request-example)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Silva <elena.silva@optumia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing export and committed tiers — next steps

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Putting short answers up front: we can deliver an anonymized per-token CSV export, and we can provide a commit-tier workbook showing effective per-token pricing and projected monthly spend at those commitment levels.

I attached a sample invoice PDF and a draft commit-pricing workbook (tab 'summary' has the three tiers you requested). Caveats:
- Bursts: committed capacity buys a lower per-token rate up to the committed volume per month; bursts above the commit are billed at a clear overage rate (we include both a blended and a marginal rate in the workbook).
- Line items: we can produce invoice-level line items either as granular per-request rows (token-level) or aggregated daily/hourly summaries; large exports are delivered as CSVs.
- Mapping: we can include your internal user IDs as a column if your calls send an identifier (service-account or app_user_id). If not, we can map by API key.

Action items:
1) Karthik — can you confirm whether the CSV schema attached matches what SE needs for integration into their cost model?
2) Marissa — I’ll need the legal OK on the overage language; can you help onboard billing/AM?

Thanks — attaching files now.

Logan Wright
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sample_invoice_lineitems.pdf] [Attachment: redwood_commit_pricing_v1.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing export and committed tiers — next steps

Looping in brief notes on the CSV schema:
- Provided columns cover what Ops/Finance usually needs: timestamp (UTC), request_id, api_key_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, cost_usd, region, request_type.
- For privacy: we often hash user identifiers before export (we include a mapping file only if the customer signs the export data agreement).
- For large historic exports (>60 days), we recommend S3 delivery rather than Drive link.

I'll also add a sample hourly-aggregate CSV if Optumia prefers summarized rows (hour, model, total_tokens, total_cost_usd).

Karthik
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

We can anonymize the sample rows — please do not include PHI.

David/Elena — attaching the requested examples:
- sample_invoice_itemized_30d.csv (anonymized, per-request rows) — shows product grouping column and request_id rows for reconciliation.
- commit_pricing_500M_breakout.xlsx — contains blended vs marginal cost columns for each incremental 100M block.
- billing_note.txt — one-paragraph language for the procurement packet.

Short answers to your numbered asks:
1) Invoice grouping: we add a top-level product code (e.g., RW-HOSTED-GEN) and then itemize by request_id for reconciliation. We include invoice_number, invoice_date, and an optional invoice_reference column you can map to internal PO numbers.
2) 500M commit: workbook tab 'marginal' shows the marginal USD per-token for 0-100M, 100-200M, etc. Blended column shows effective per-token rate across the full 500M.
3) Billing note (copyable): "Committed tokens are reserved capacity billed monthly against the agreed commit. Unused committed tokens at the end of a billing quarter may be rolled forward up to one subsequent quarter with prior notice; otherwise, unused tokens are forfeited. Refunds are only issued in the event of billing errors or contract termination under section 5.3 of the Master Services Agreement."

Next step: if the finance team is happy with the CSV schema and the commit workbook, I can have our billing team generate a draft invoice and draft SOW language for the commit. Marissa — can you flag the legal/billing folks?

Thanks,
Logan
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
